propositions: A configured provider is silently discarded when the model id contains a colon, because _resolve_target treats any colon as proof of an already-qualified string
Canonical Bedrock model ids in the form 'us.anthropic.claude-…-v1:0' contain a colon in the version suffix, not as a provider separator, causing them to fail resolution while unversioned aliases work
An explicitly configured provider must be checked first before scanning the model string for qualifiers, so no punctuation in a model id can overrule an explicit instruction

A conflicting pair of configured provider and inline qualifier (e.g. 'openai:gpt-4o' with provider='bedrock') must raise rather than silently pick a winner, because either choice discards an explicit instruction

The qualified/unqualified decision was implemented twice independently (_resolve_target and infer_provider) allowing them to drift, now unified in split_provider_qualifier with a shape-based test on provider prefix format
